ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory cross-screening of all shareholders, directors, and UBOs against: (a) the Egyptian Central Bank of Egypt sanctions and terrorist financing lists; (b) United Nations Security Council consolidated list; (c) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list and sectoral sanctions; (d) European Union consolidated financial sanctions list; (e) domestic politically exposed persons (PEP) registers maintained by Egyptian supervisory authorities. Enhanced due diligence applies to PEPs, higher-risk jurisdictions, and politically-active family members. All screening must be documented contemporaneously and retained for at least five years under Law No. 80/2016.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones) online Name Reservation Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company name must be in Arabic for the Arabic-language version of the incorporation file. A Latin-script transliteration is permitted for foreign trade and customs usage, but the Arabic name controls for statutory purposes. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any registered entity in Egypt. When a foreign corporate shareholder's name is used, the Arabic transliteration must preserve the phonic identity of the original legal name and must not form an Arabic word with an unintended public-order meaning.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Misleading medical or pharmaceutical terms such as 'Dialysis Center' or 'Hospital' when the entity is a manufacturer and not a licensed healthcare provider
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of receiving GAFI's written name rejection, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal via GAFI's central legal department. The appeal must include the reserved name, the objection reasons, a legal memorandum explaining why the proposed name is not prohibited, and any supporting trademark registration certificates or letters of no-objection from prior rights holders. GAFI must issue a reasoned decision; if the appeal fails, the applicant may bring a challenge before the Egyptian Administrative Court within the statutory judicial review period, typically 60 days from notification.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for a medical device manufacturing company. A physical commercial office or industrial facility is mandatory for GAFI registration, Egyptian Drug Authority pre-licensing inspections, and the Ministry of Industry's industrial license. A virtual office may be used only as a secondary administrative address after the primary registered office physically exists.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (75% estimated likelihood within the first operating year). The Egyptian Drug Authority, Ministry of Health, and GAFI may conduct unannounced physical inspections because the company will manufacture Class II/III medical devices (dialysis hemodialyzers) that require compliance with ISO 13485, GMP, and Egyptian Medical Devices Authority requirements.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 on Joint Stock, Limited Partnership and Limited Liability Companies, as amended, Articles 102–112 (LLC formation and management); Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; Commercial Registration Law No. 34 of 1976.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Foreign Trade (GAFI) — Companies Registration One-Stop Shop; Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Trade and Industry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Arabic Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association, submitted through the GAFI One-Stop Shop with the statutory incorporation application form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed on an Egyptian LLC. The memorandum fixes the share capital, which is divided into equal shares, and each share must be paid in cash or in kind before Commercial Registry issuance. GAFI practice requires evidence of capital availability in a provisional bank account opened in the Company’s name; the funds are released after incorporation is completed. No formal escrow account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that each founding shareholder subscribes to the allotted number of shares in the Company’s stated capital and agrees to pay the same into the Company’s provisional bank account as required by applicable Egyptian law; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is adopted at [premises address, city, Egypt] and the lease/title documents are authorized for filing; RESOLVED, that the managers (directors) of the Company are constituted. WHEREAS, [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer and [Name] as General Financial Manager, with authority, acting jointly or severally, to execute the incorporation filings, open bank accounts, engage counsel, and fulfill all statutory obligations. All Resolutions are effective immediately upon adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Notarization of Constituent Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI/EgyBiz one-stop shop and the Public Notary or GAFI legalization office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name clearance request through EgyBiz, obtain Commercial Registry approval, then have all founding shareholders sign the Arabic Memorandum and Articles before a notary public; legalize signatures as required by GAFI.
required_dossiers: Name clearance certificate from the Commercial Registry/GAFI
Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association in Arabic (notarized draft)
Valid national ID or passport copies of all founding shareholders
Notarized power of attorney for each foreign founder, certified by the Egyptian Consulate if executed abroad
Company incorporation request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name clearance is refused, resubmit an alternate proposed name within five working days; if notarization is rejected due to signature discrepancy, correct the identity documents and re-notarize.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI Companies Registration Department / One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized constituent documents together with the GAFI incorporation application; pay statutory fees; provide the bank capital deposit certificate if requested; await GAFI decision and issuance of the incorporation approval certificate.
required_dossiers: Notarized Memorandum and Articles (three copies)
Name reservation and Commercial Registry clearance certificate
Provisional bank capital deposit certificate or share subscription payment proof
Founding shareholders' passport/ID copies
Managers/directors acceptance of office
Lease contract or title deed of the registered office
GAFI incorporation application form and legal representation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a remarks sheet, cure by amending the constituent documents to comply with the Investment Law and resubmit through the One-Stop Shop within 30 calendar days; an objection may be filed with the GAFI Legal Complaints Committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Registration and Tax/Social Insurance Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry (Ministry of Trade and Industry); Egyptian Tax Authority; General Authority for Social Insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After GAFI approval, submit the incorporation certificate to the Commercial Registry for the company extract; register for the Tax Identification Number/Tax Card, value added tax position, and social insurance for the establishment and employees.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation approval certificate
Notarized Memorandum and Articles
Commercial Registry application form
Certificate of capital deposit / paid-up capital declaration
Registered office lease or title deed
Manager appointment resolution
Tax card application and legal representative ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry queries the extract, file corrective statements with GAFI and the notary and re-present; for tax card delays, escalate through the Egyptian Tax Authority service office to its complaint window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI aftercare; Commercial Registry; corporate legal counsel/notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify publication of the formation summary if required; issue share certificates to the founding shareholders; open the statutory meetings book, members ledger, and accounting records; adopt the company seal and activate the operating bank account.
required_dossiers: GAFI incorporation certificate and Commercial Registry extract
First board resolution appointing officers and adopting the registered office
Shareholders ledger and statutory books templates
Company seal/chop specimen
Bank account activation forms and board mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is objected to, file the registration proof with the registry and pay any late publication surcharge; correct share certificate wording to match the memorandum and reissue.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Industrial Development Authority (IDA), Ministry of Trade and Industry, and the Egyptian Drug Authority (EDA) for medical device establishment and product licensing; local governorate industrial zone authorities for land and building certification.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Factory Establishment and Operation License under the Industrial Development Law No. 150 of 2009, together with the EDA Manufacturer Establishment License and product registration certificate for disposable dialysis hemofilters (polyethersulfone hollow-fiber dialyzers).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B / List II: initial Environmental Impact Assessment screening and registration required before construction; a full Environmental Impact Assessment report is required if wet extrusion capacity or solvent recovery exceeds prescribed thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must satisfy Law 93/1962 and Ministerial Decree 44/2015 limits (e.g., BOD ≤ 300 mg/l, COD ≤ 500 mg/l, TSS ≤ 250 mg/l, pH 6–9). Air emissions and volatile organic compounds must comply with Law 4/1994 as amended by Law 9/2009 and Prime Ministerial Decree No. 338/2011. Waste, including rejected polyethersulfone membranes, must be classified and disposed of under Law No. 202 of 2020 and EDA medical waste guidelines.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Civil Defense Department (Ministry of Interior) after inspection of extrusion, potting, packaging, and cleanroom areas; municipal structural load and building safety clearance; occupational health and safety registration with the Ministry of Manpower under Law No. 12 of 2003; and cleanroom validation per ISO 14644 appropriate for manufacture of sterile dialysis filters.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; official online portal at https://www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity shall submit the unified tax registration application to the ETA, attaching notarized and legalized certificate of incorporation, articles of association, proof of local registered address, board resolution on local representative, power of attorney, passport copies of authorized signatories, and local bank account details; the ETA verifies the file and issues the Tax Identification Number (TIN) and separate VAT registration number where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity election exists under Egyptian law; an LLC is mandatorily taxed as a corporate entity at entity level, while certain investment incentive elections and special economic zone tax regimes may be separately approved by the General Authority for Investment (GAFI).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration is triggered when annual taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000; producers/exporters may also be required to register irrespective of turnover if export activities generate recoverable input VAT claims.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: VAT-registered enterprises must integrate certified billing software with the ETA e-invoicing system; invoices and e-receipts are transmitted in real time to the ETA in XML or JSON formats, the ETA validates and clears each document, returns a unique invoice UUID, digital signature, and machine-readable QR code; rejected or tampered invoices are deemed non-compliant and attract administrative penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of exported goods are zero-rated where the taxpayer proves the goods physically left Egypt under customs supervision, holds valid export declarations and transport documents, receives the sale price in hard currency through an Egyptian bank, and submits the export-related evidence with the VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill,
Packing List and certificate of origin where required,
Inward Remittance Certificate / Foreign Exchange Receipt confirming hard-currency repatriation
Bank/Letter of Credit payment evidence (Swift MT700/MT103)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and customs authorities may retrospectively audit export zero-rating files; failure to substantiate physical export or to repatriate proceeds within the statutory deadline invalidates the zero rate, resulting in assessment of VAT at 14%, late-payment interest, and administrative fines; fraudulent claims for zero-rating or export refunds may trigger criminal penalties including imprisonment and fines up to the amount of tax evaded.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE), acting through its Foreign Exchange Operations, Banking Control and Anti-Money Laundering supervisory sectors under Law No. 194 of 2020 on the Central Bank and the Banking System, together with the Ministry of Investment (GAFI) for FDI registration and the Egyptian Drug Authority for medical-device trade veracity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Egyptian pound (EGP) is convertible for genuine current-account transactions (trade invoices, freight, insurance and post-audit profit remittances), while the capital account remains controlled: inward FDI is freely registrable, but outbound capital items such as equity divestment proceeds, shareholder loan repayments and liquidation distributions require CBE documentary vetting and may be queued during interbank liquidity stress. Profit remittance to the non-resident shareholder is permitted without CBE pre-approval once the handling bank verifies (i) audited financial statements, (ii) full settlement of corporate income tax and the 5% dividend withholding regime, and (iii) a valid notarised distribution resolution; practical hurdles include a 3-to-5 business-day FX execution window, bank-level source-of-funds statements and possible deferral under CBE priority settlement rules. Since the March 2024 unified float, interbank pricing reflects market supply and demand, but full capital mobility cannot be assumed outside normal trade cycles.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory repatriation deadline: export proceeds from dialysis hemofilter sales must be collected through an authorised Egyptian bank within 180 calendar days from the bill-of-lading or airway-bill date, or within one month of contractual maturity for open-account and deferred-payment terms; regulated medical consumables are frequently policed on a 90-day bank-internal target. Mandatory conversion ratio: under the post-March 2024 flexible exchange-rate framework, the CBE no longer enforces a blanket 100% EGP surrender requirement; up to 100% of export receipts may be retained in a monitored foreign-currency account when the exporter submits a CBE-compliant FX retention budget linked to documented import expenditures (polyethersulfone polymer, polycarbonate housings, sterilisation and freight costs). Where no retention plan is approved, the authorised bank will convert 100% at the daily interbank rate; non-repatriation triggers CBE export-default registry sanctions, loss of trade-finance limits and Article 207 Law No. 194/2020 penalties.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EGP/USD master account and export-proceeds retention sub-ledger)
Operational Account (multi-currency current account with EGP conversion line)
Capital Escrow Account (FDI cash subscription) plus Operational Account
Operational Account (hard-currency concentration and documentary LC issuance desk)
Operational Account (specialised trade-finance facility and treasury products)
Operational Account (local payroll, tax-payment and EGP clearing rail)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW / NOT VIABLE as the LLC's primary treasury or clearing account. Egypt's payment-systems regulation (Law No. 18 of 2019) and CBE licensing rules do not recognise offshore fintech e-money institutions for EGP-denominated balances, local payroll, supplier settlements, tax payments, export-proceeds collection or import trade settlement; EGP is non-deliverable outside Egypt and all inward export dollars must be routed to a CBE-licensed bank for customs and export-incentive matching. An overseas FCA- or EMI-licensed wallet may be used by the foreign parent only for incidental offshore vendor payments and must never book the Egyptian subsidiary's operational revenue or capital contributions.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-branch biometric verification is compulsory for the resident Egyptian signatory (general manager or attorney-in-fact) at initial account opening. Non-resident directors and ultimate beneficial owners may complete the dossier through apostilled powers of attorney and an electronic video call where CBE e-KYC guidelines are adopted; however, most tier-1 Egyptian banks retain a substantive interview requirement for the UBO and will reject a purely remote onboarding for a foreign-controlled LLC, requiring either a physical visit to the branch or attendance at the Egyptian embassy in the UBO's jurisdiction for signature witnessing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-tier non-resident ownership with UBO holding shares indirectly through Gulf-based trusts or intermediate companies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled chain-of-title file containing certificates of incorporation of each holding layer, GAFI investment certificate, the LLC's notarised register of members, UBO declarations under Egyptian AML Law No. 80/2002, sworn source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements, audited parent financial statements for the last two fiscal years and two bank references from the UBO's home jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Medical consumable export patterns inconsistent with unit economics, such as repeated split shipments of high-value dialysers to high-risk MENA transshipment hubs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade dossier: pro-forma invoices and purchase orders; LC or MT103 documentary trail; packing lists and air-waybills matched to each shipment; ISO 13485 / CE-MDR certification, US FDA 510(k) or Egyptian Drug Authority registration for the hemofilter; sterilisation and release certificates; end-user and consignee declarations; distributor due-diligence files; and a business-substance package comprising factory lease, payroll history, utility bills and customs manifest archive.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Immediate onshore cycling of incoming hard currency from capital escrow to EGP operating account with no matching operating expenditure, creating an AML layering flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBE-standard rolling 12-month foreign-currency budget and EGP liquidity forecast; share-subscription schedule and board minutes earmarking capital for construction and equipment; pro-forma capex quotations, import LC drafts and payroll summaries; recent Egyptian Tax Authority clearance certificate and audited financial statements demonstrating that the capital is consumed in fixed assets and working capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential export-control or counterfeit-medical-device scrutiny arising from dual-use production equipment (hollow-fibre spinning and potting lines) sourced from restricted suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Equipment import licences from the Egyptian Customs Authority and Egyptian Drug Authority; supplier commercial and export licences with Incoterms-consistent purchase contracts; utilisation declaration and capacity plan for the spinning line; local inspection report and pharmaceutical-affairs No Objection letters; end-user undertaking that the machinery will remain installed at the registered manufacturing address.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign shareholder initiates a SWIFT MT103 from its home bank to the Egyptian bank's USD/EUR nostro account, populating Field 70 with the remittance reason 'INWARD CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION - EGYPT LLC - GAFI FILE NO.' and Field 72 with the LLC's TIN and bank account IBAN. The Egyptian bank screens the remittance against CBE sanctions lists, matches it to the inward remittance declaration submitted by the company, and credits the capital-escrow account; the credit is then converted domestically to EGP at the interbank rate or retained in USD according to the approved retention budget. The LLC must pre-file the GAFI investment update, a board resolution accepting the subscription, a share-issuance schedule and source-of-funds supporting documents; amounts above USD 500,000 trigger enhanced due diligence and a potential one-to-two business-day compliance hold. The receiving bank issues a certificate of inward remittance, which is later used for dividend matching and capital-repatriation evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Input-material procurement (polyethersulfone granules, PU potting resin, polycarbonate case shells and sterile packaging) is cleared through: (i) confirmed irrevocable documentary letters of credit issued by the Egyptian bank under UCP 600, advised via SWIFT MT700/MT710 and settled through MT103/MT202 after compliant negotiation; (ii) documentary collections D/P or D/A under URC 522 for trusted EU and US suppliers; or (iii) advance-payment wire transfers via SWIFT MT103 for low-value repeat purchases under USD 25,000. The company must maintain an import tax card, Egyptian Drug Authority import licence for regulated medical-grade input codes, customs declarations through NAFIZA, and import payments are settled in USD/EUR through the bank's correspondent rails (Deutsche Bank, JPMorgan, HSBC, Commerzbank) without touching the offshore EGP market; domestic EGP payroll, tax and liquidity disbursements run onshore through CBE RTGS from the operational account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright USD/EGP forward contracts (tenors 90-180 days) booked by the Egyptian LLC with a CBE-licensed treasury bank, permitted only when backed by a firm underlying import invoice, export LC or audited cash-flow exposure; extensions and margin top-ups follow CBE derivative margin rules.

Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP principal-exchange swaps) with the main clearing bank to bridge the capital-escrow period and operational-account EGP needs, subject to ISDA/CSA netting, CBE reporting and a documented non-speculative treasury mandate.

Offshore EGP non-deliverable forward (NDF) overlay permissible solely at the level of the foreign parent company to hedge translation and equity exposure; the Egyptian LLC itself must not enter an NDF, and any offshore settlement must occur in USD outside CBE territory with no onshore EGP refunding leg.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (CIT) — Form No. 20, with audited financial statements (balance sheet, P&L) annexed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) — Central Income Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months following fiscal year-end; calendar-year entity: on or before 30 April
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: fine equal to 10% of due tax (Art. 72, Income Tax Law 91/2005). Late payment: additional tax of 2% per month or part-month of delay (Art. 73). Non-filing triggers ex officio assessment and administrative enforcement; persistent default exposes the entity to registry strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Three interim CIT advance payments (دفعات مقدمة) — each installment equal to one-third of the preceding year's final CIT liability
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year entity: installments due 30 April, 31 July and 31 October of the current tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Each late installment accrues the statutory 2% monthly additional tax (Art. 73, Law 91/2005) and may be collected by garnishment/administrative attachment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the Commercial Register entry (تجديد القيد بالسجل التجاري) and issuance of renewed registration certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry Office at the company's domicile — Ministry of Trade and Industry; GAFI coordinates for ETA-registered investors
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: During the calendar month corresponding to the anniversary of initial commercial registration each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-renewal fines under Commercial Registry Law 34/1976; official warning followed by administrative strike-off (شطب) of the registry record; directors face continued-trading liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ordinary General Assembly: approval of audited annual financial statements, auditor reappointment and discharge of managers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI / Companies Registrar — minutes signed into the company's statutory minute book; no general government filing fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within 6 months of fiscal year-end; calendar-year entity: on or before 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EGP 5,000–20,000 for violation of Companies Law 159/1981; managers denied civil discharge; repeated failure permits GAFI to apply for judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly VAT return and payment (Form 79/electronic return via ETA portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the end of each calendar month (e.g., January return by end of February)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing fine EGP 500–50,000 per return; late payment additional tax 2% per month (VAT Law 67/2016, Arts. 41 and 43); input credit blocked during default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Payroll final-withholding annual reconciliation (salaries tax) and employer annual statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority — Payroll/Employment Tax Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual salary-tax reconciliation covering the prior calendar year due by 31 January of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Withholding agent liable for unremitted WHT plus 2% monthly delay surcharge; individual tax card non-issuance sanctions under Law 91/2005.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% on taxable corporate profits of Egyptian LLCs under Law No. 91/2005 as amended
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Investment Law No. 72/2017 permits a 50% investment allowance on qualifying capital expenditures over 5 years, reduced CIT rates for newly established SMEs, and 0% CIT on eligible export-oriented profits for companies operating inside licensed public free zones; a standard non-free-zone dialysis consumables manufacturer may use the investment allowance and standard deductions, but not a statutory holiday

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egypt Corporate Income Tax Return Form 19 for Limited Liability Companies, filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal (www.eta.gov.eg)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The CIT return must be filed within 4 months of the end of the fiscal year, unless the ETA has granted a written extension; the fiscal year is the entity’s accounting year as declared in Egypt

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: name, tax registration number, tax card number, commercial registration number, and activity code (ISIC/ETA activity classification)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete only with the Egyptian permanent establishment (PE) tax card and branch registration data if the non-resident operates through a PE in Egypt

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting basis and audited financial statements annex: balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes under Egyptian Accounting Standards or IFRS as adopted
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Egyptian branch audited financial statements and the head office allocation statement of Egyptian-source taxable profits or losses

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue and gross receipts: domestic and export sales of disposable dialysis hemofilters and related medical consumables, adjusted for rebates and discounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only include Egyptian-source revenue of the PE or sales attributable to exploitation of assets/trade in Egypt; intercompany export transactions must be shown at arm's length

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income and non-deductible expenses: free-zone profit declarations, dividends received, realized capital gains under incentive provisions, entertainment and penalties disallowed
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim treaty-exempt business profits only if the DTA attributes no permanent establishment in Egypt; attach the relevant DTA article and TRC

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory deductions and investment allowances: manufacturing overheads, direct material and labor, utility costs, depreciation, R&D, 50% investment allowance, donations within caps
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PE deductions are limited to expenses actually incurred for the Egyptian PE; head office expenses are deductible only if correctly allocated and documented

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from prior years: evidence of original loss year, amount, and remaining five-year carryforward position
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PE may carry forward Egyptian PE losses in accordance with Law 91/2005; losses of an exempt foreign head office cannot be offset against Egyptian PE profit

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base computation: accounting profit plus non-deductible expenses minus exempt income minus tax loss carryforward, resulting in statutory taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same computation as a resident company; transfer pricing adjustments must be reflected in the taxable base before applying the 22.5% rate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable at 22.5%, less advance tax payments, tax credits, and withholding tax credits; the balance is the due CIT with any claim for refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-residents subject to withholding on dividends/interest/royalties, do not include those payments in the PE form unless the payments are attributable to the Egyptian PE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transfer pricing declaration: full disclosure of related-party transactions including export sales of hemofilters to foreign affiliates, purchases of hollow fiber membranes, royalties, management fees, and financing
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident group members issuing transfer pricing invoices must attach a TRC and, where threshold is exceeded, the group’s Master File/Local File for the Egyptian PE

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or late submission of required annexes exposes the company to a fixed fine of up to EGP 20,000 under Law 91/2005, plus a monthly delay surcharge equal to 2% of the unpaid tax for each month or fraction of a month up to 100% of the tax; inaccurate returns with demonstrable intent attract tax evasion penalties and criminal sanctions

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding tax on dividend distributions paid by an Egyptian LLC to shareholders; the tax applies to both resident and non-resident payees and is withheld from the gross dividend at distribution
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke an Egypt double tax agreement, the beneficial owner must present a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) to the paying Egyptian company before the distribution; the paying company may apply the reduced DTA rate or exemption only after the ETA accepts the Mutual Agreement Procedure exemption/relief form or the payer obtains an advance tax instruction; otherwise the 10% statutory WHT is withheld and the non-resident must file an ETA refund application with the TRC, audited beneficial-ownership declaration, and supporting DTA article
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Egyptian withholding tax is 20% on interest payments and 20% on royalty or IP-licensing payments made to non-residents; DTA rates may reduce these to between 0% and 15% depending on the treaty partner, the nature of the payment, and the recipient's beneficial ownership, subject to the same TRC and ETA approval procedure

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A mandatory contemporaneous Local File must be prepared and filed on request where the aggregate value of related-party transactions exceeds EGP 10 million in the tax year; a group Master File is required where the group-wide related-party transaction volume or group revenue exceeds ETA-specified thresholds in the same annual guidance; all taxpayers must complete the TP disclosure annex irrespective of the threshold
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not yet maintain a stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations statute comparable to Gulf Cooperation Council jurisdictions, but the ETA applies OECD substance-over-form and the Investment Law operational requirements: an LLC deriving tax treaty benefits, free-zone exemptions, or investment incentives must have real premises, employees, and actual manufacturing activity in Egypt; a letter-box company or conduit arrangement without economic substance is treated as a sham for tax purposes and is denied treaty relief, incentives, and related-party deductions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of manufacturing revenues, fabrication of invoices for dialysis consumables, fictitious export documents, omission of export commission income, or false declaration of the ISIC 3250 manufacturing activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under Law 91/2005 carries imprisonment for 3 to 5 years plus a fine ranging from EGP 100,000 to EGP 5,000,000; the ETA may additionally reassess the hidden tax and impose the 2% monthly delay surcharge and 100% cap
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed false returns are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax, the fines, and civil restitution; Egyptian courts may issue travel bans and asset freezes and, upon conviction, impose the same imprisonment penalty on directors

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Manipulating intercompany prices for hollow fiber membranes, dialyzer potting services, royalty fees, or export distribution margins to shift profit to a foreign low-tax affiliate, failing to file the TP disclosure annex, refusing to present the Local/Master File after ETA request, or failing to apply the arm's length standard
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA issues a transfer pricing adjustment, disallows excessive related-party deductions, and imposes the unpaid tax with the 2% monthly delay surcharge, plus a documentation penalty of up to EGP 50,000 under the ETA administrative penalty framework; severe factual falsification is treated as tax evasion with fines and imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Executives and in-house accountants who engineered the mispricing may be held personally liable for the entire adjusted tax difference, disgorgement of diverted profits, and criminal culpability; directors may be banned from leaving Egypt pending settlement of the TP assessment

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Egyptian LLC as a nominee or conduit that holds legal title to the dialysis manufacturing contract but has no physical premises, no qualified staff, no PES membrane extrusion or potting operations, and no commercial risk, solely to obtain Egyptian treaty benefits or free-zone incentives for a foreign principal
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ETA disregards the entity for tax purposes, denies treaty benefits and investment incentives, taxes the income at the full 22.5% in the name of the true owner, and imposes a 2% monthly delay penalty and criminal fines under the anti-abuse articles of Law 91/2005; the company's free-zone license may be revoked by the General Authority for Investment and the customs duty benefits recovered
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee shareholders and directors who enabled the conduit arrangement risk veil-piercing under Egyptian company law, joint and several liability for tax debts, civil damages for commercial fraud, travel bans, and imprisonment for participation in an unlawful structure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, Foreign Exchange, and Custom Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving export proceeds through non-bank channels, settling invoices through unlicensed money remitters, concealing beneficial ownership of the non-resident parent, or materially under-invoicing exports to evade customs valuation and Egypt's foreign exchange repatriation rules
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law No. 80/2002 and Egyptian anti-money laundering amendments, the offense is punishable by imprisonment of 1 to 7 years and fines from EGP 100,000 to EGP 1,000,000; customs violations draw additional penalties equal to several times the evaded duty and confiscation of goods
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers may be jailed for money laundering facilitation, fined personally, restrained from traveling, and ordered by court to repatriate the offshore funds; the LLC may be dissolved as a non-operational shell after repeated violations
